newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-GENTLER AUGUSTA NATIONAL FOR EARLY SECOND ROUND STARTERS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-GENTLER AUGUSTA NATIONAL FOR EARLY SECOND ROUND STARTERS.

text.p: A gentler Augusta National on Friday greeted early second round starters, some still shell-shocked from Thursday's brutal opening round of the Masters.
Warmer temperatures and soft breezes replaced the chill winds of Thursday and pin placements were not as penal, giving players a fighting chance at survival on Augusta's hard, racetrack fast greens.

No one was yet mounting a charge to worry first-round leader John Huston, whose miracle eagle on the 18th hole Thursday landed him in first place with a five-under score of 67. But there were indications that scoring would improve.
A forecast of rain for Friday night gave beleaguered golfers hope that Mother Nature would intervene to soften up the putting surfaces for the weekend.
Charles Coody, 59, had an easier time, making the turn at one-over-par and adding an eagle-three on the 13th hole. He shot 83 in the first round.
Ken Green, whose first round of 87 featured six three-putts, one four-putt and one five-putt, got to even-par for the day through 15 holes before sliding back with bogeys on the last two holes.

Scott Hoch, runner-up to Nick Faldo in a playoff for the Masters crown in 1989, shot 79 to open the tournament but used an eagle-three on the par-5 second hole to make the turn Friday in two-under 34.
Greg Norman, last year's runner-up, had a tap-in birdie on the first hole and was one-under for the day after seven holes following his opening 77.
The 86-man field averaged more than 76 on the par-72 layout in the first round, which saw 16 "others" -- scores worse than double-bogey -- posted.
Some players, however, had every bit as tough a time.

Arnold Palmer, playing his 43rd consecutive Masters despite undergoing surgery for prostate cancer in January, shot 44 on each side Friday to go along with his first-round 89 for his worst ever Augusta scoring.
Loren Roberts, one of the tour's best putters, followed his opening 85 with a weak 77.
Green, who played with Palmer Friday, said the greens felt friendlier than they had in Thursday's nightmare round.
"They're slower now. You'll see a lot better scores today," Green said. "Today Augusta is like it usually is. Yesterday was a little bizarre."
